definition: In this historical psychological usage, working backward means reasoning from fully formed experience to an earlier, more undifferentiated mental whole from which later distinctions develop. It refers to tracing mental development back to a theoretical objective continuum rather than explaining mind as built up from originally separate elements.

provenance.revision: 1901 New York Macmillan original; archive index checked 2026-10-18
provenance.scope: Source record Continuum; pinned source text

reasons: The definition claims that “working backward means reasoning from fully formed experience to an earlier… mental whole,” but the packet does not describe “fully formed experience” in those terms; it instead says differentiation runs “back to a theoretical state” “before specific experience.”

The definition’s wording about an “earlier, more undifferentiated mental whole” is broadly consistent with the packet’s “undifferentiated field” and “totum obiectivum/objective continuum,” but the specific formulation “fully formed experience” is not supported by the supplied text.
